CONTENT:

Agra Fort is located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India. The walled imperial city of the Mughals in Agra, rebuilt in red sandstone by Emperor Akbar from 1565 and later embellished in white marble by Shah Jahan.

History of Agra Fort. The official Agra district tourism page describes Agra Fort as the walled imperia
title: Agra Fort

text:
ism page describes Agra Fort as the walled imperial city of the Mughals and states that Emperor Akbar rebuilt it in red sandstone from 1565, with later white-marble additions by Shah Jahan.

Architecture of Agra Fort. The fort's 2.5-kilometre ramparts enclose structures including Jahangir Mahal, Khas Mahal, Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Sheesh Mahal, Musamman Burj and Moti Masjid.

History of Akbar's Tomb (Sikandra). The official Agra district tourism page says the mausoleum was begun by Akbar and completed by his s
title: Akbar's Tomb (Sikandra)

text:
ausoleum was begun by Akbar and completed by his son Jahangir in 1613. It stands in a 119-acre charbagh at Sikandra.

Architecture of Akbar's Tomb (Sikandra). The five-storeyed sandstone-and-marble pyramid and its gateway combine Hindu, Islamic and Persian motifs, according to the official Agra district tourism page.

History of Fatehpur Sikri. The official Agra district tourism page states that Akbar f
title: Fatehpur Sikri

text:
ial Agra district tourism page states that Akbar founded Fatehpur Sikri in 1571 and that it served as the Mughal capital for about 14 years.

Architecture of Fatehpur Sikri. The complex includes Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid, the marble Tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti, Panch Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas and Jodha Bai's Palace. The district page describes a blend of Persian, Hindu and Jain architectural idioms.

Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh) is located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India. Mughal garden in Agra, also known as Aram Bagh.

History of Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh). The garden is attributed to Emperor Babur and dated to 1526. Babur was temporarily buried there before his remains were moved to Kabul.

History of Taj Mahal. The Taj Mahal was commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal. Construction began around 1632. The main mausoleum was completed around 1648, while additional elements of the complex were completed by 1653. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
